title: Connect enables in-page Renown sign-in via connect.renown.switchboardUrl plus rainbow/privy adapters
content:
## Redirect by default, in-page by config

By default Connect authenticates by **redirecting** the user to the Renown portal to connect a wallet and mint the credential, then returning to the app. In-page sign-in — pick a login method inside Connect, sign the credential there, written and logged in via Switchboard without leaving the app — is opt-in and configured entirely through `powerhouse.config.json`.

- **`connect.renown.switchboardUrl`** — the Switchboard GraphQL endpoint. When set, Connect *attempts* in-page sign-in. When absent, or when no wallet session can be produced, Connect falls back to the redirect flow automatically, so nothing breaks if it is left unset.
- **`connect.renown.adapters`** — presence of a key enables that adapter.

```json
"renown": {
  "url": "https://www.renown.id",
  "switchboardUrl": "https://switchboard.example/graphql",
  "adapters": {
    "rainbow": { "walletConnectProjectId": "..." },
    "privy": { "appId": "...", "methods": ["google", "email"] }
  }
}
```

## The two adapters

**`rainbow`** (`{ walletConnectProjectId }`) — external wallets via RainbowKit + wagmi. Treat `walletConnectProjectId` as **required in practice**: without it only an installed browser wallet (or a Safe App iframe) can sign in, because every other RainbowKit wallet connects over the WalletConnect relay, which needs a project id. Those wallets are omitted rather than offered and failing.

**`privy`** (`{ appId, clientId?, methods? }`) — embedded wallets plus social/email login. `methods` defaults to `["google", "email"]`. Social and email login run inside Privy's own modal, with OAuth in a popup so the page stays alive. Each method must be enabled in the Privy dashboard with Connect's origin allowlisted.

## Two operational notes

Only **public** identifiers belong in the config — a Privy **App Secret** is server-only and must never appear in `powerhouse.config.json`. And each adapter's wallet library is fetched only on the first login click, so enabling in-page auth adds nothing to startup cost; Connect ships with every adapter's peer dependencies installed, so operators only edit config.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/03-Build/03-BuildingUserExperiences/07-Authorization/01-RenownAuthenticationFlow.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Presence of switchboardUrl opts into in-page sign-in; without it Connect falls back to the redirect flow. Adapters are keyed rainbow and privy in powerhouse.config.json.
